finding.claim: Blind SSRF through the webhook callback URL. Any caller of POST /subscribe can register an arbitrary URL. The server then sends a POST request to that URL every minute. Targets can include loopback, internal services, and cloud metadata endpoints such as http://169.254.169.254/. The payload is sent as the request body. The response body is read but not returned, so the SSRF is blind. The recurring request is the impact.
finding.source: callbackUrl body parameter of POST /subscribe (Jobs.subscribe, line 13)

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-supplied URL
URL stored unvalidated in the subscriptions map
notifyAll iterates the stored callback URLs on the minute job
URI.create(cb) builds the request with no scheme or host check
HttpClient sends the POST to the attacker-chosen host

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, no host or IP allowlist, no private, loopback or link-local blocking, and no DNS pinning. No auth check is visible on subscribe, though only this file exists. HttpClient.newHttpClient() does not follow redirects by default, but that does not mitigate a direct internal URL.

verdict.reason: Jobs.java:13-14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and Jobs.java:19-24 POSTs to URI.create(cb) with no scheme/host check (the only regex guard is in thumb() at line 30, a different path), and no auth exists in the only file present.
